The entry's "medium impact / already-better / done" framing overstates completion: it is better-in-check, loop-wiring-unfinished. The tradeoffs field half-senses this ("reliant on validate_math being run") but still asserts the three-channel reach.)
- **Invariant check:** HTML-only is the invariant itself; validate_math is read-only, located, and never writes source. Directly upholds the fixed invariants.

### D165. Ship static accessibility linting as an advisory, click-to-source warning class, split by what is block-model-knowable vs computed-CSS, and give it a real warn-vs-fail severity tier (Proposed (revised))

- **Impact:** medium, **confidence:** medium, **skeptic verdict:** revise
- **Quarto does:** Quarto ships no document accessibility linter at all. `quarto check` verifies only the toolchain (Pandoc, Deno, R/Python/Jupyter, LaTeX, TinyTeX), never the rendered document. Quarto supports `fig-alt` on figures and emits reasonably semantic HTML, but nothing in the pipeline flags an alt-less raw `<img>`, a heading-level skip, an unnamed icon-only link or button, or a contrast miss. Accessibility is left entirely to the author and to external tools (axe, WAVE, Lighthouse) run after publish, on the built HTML, out of band from the authoring loop.
- **Critique:** Taliesin claims to run "the same" a11y rule set in two places that actually disagree on both severity and coverage. In the live preview `scanA11y` (web-client/client.js) the findings are explicitly advisory and "never block rendering," rendered as dismissable panel rows. In the kernel-free `check` gate the identical findings become plain `Warning`s, and `check` exits non-zero on ANY warning (check.rs:294), so one hand-written alt-less `<img>` hard-fails a CI build exactly like a dangling cross-reference or a missing asset. `Warning` has no severity field (only message/file/line at model.rs:146), so a11y advisories cannot be told apart from correctness errors. Coverage also diverges: contrast (needs computed CSS) and `<html lang>` (needs the page shell) run only client-side, so a headless `check` silently vouches for strictly LESS a11y than the author sees in the preview, and contrast, the single highest-impact rule, is exactly the one the gate cannot assert.
- **Quarto's strongest defense:** Quarto is a multi-format compiler (HTML, PDF, docx, ePub, revealjs). Accessibility semantics are format-specific, and for HTML the accessibility tree a real audit needs (computed color/contrast, ARIA accessible-name computation, focus order, live regions) only exists in a browser after CSS and scripts apply. The mature, standards-tracking tools that already encode the full, evolving WCAG ruleset (axe-core, WAVE, Lighthouse, pa11y) run exactly there and are continuously maintained. A source-time linter inside the compiler can only see a partial static slice, so shipping one invites two failure modes Quarto reasonably refuses: false confidence (green check reads as certified-accessible) and false positives that train authors to ignore the warning. Quarto instead spends its budget on prevention (semantic HTML by default, first-class fig-alt, ARIA in its own components) and delegates verification to the specialized ecosystem run on the built artifact. Make the default accessible, let dedicated browser-based tools verify: that is a defensible, low-false-confidence division of labor, not negligence. Note this steelman also sharpens the highest-value a11y check (contrast) as precisely the one that needs a browser, which is why the weakest part of the Taliesin proposal is trying to statically reproduce it.
- **Taliesin today:** `crates/core/src/diagnostics/a11y.rs::validate_a11y(blocks, format)` ships three static, kernel-free rules over the rendered block model: (1) mid-document heading-level skip of >=2 (never "must start at h1"; decks exempt), (2) interactive element with no accessible name, covering `<a href>`/`<button>` plus `role="button"|"link"|"tab"` on non-native elements like `<div role="button">`, and (3) a raw `<img>` with no `alt` (markdown `![]()` always emits one, so this catches hand-written HTML only). Each finding is a `Warning` with file+line on the shared click-to-source channel, run by `taliesin check` (crates/server/src/check.rs) beside the other validators and pinned by `corpus/diagnostics/a11y.qmd` plus tests `corpus_a11y_pin_doc_trips_each_rule_through_check` and `collect_diagnostics_surfaces_a11y_rules`. The live preview runs a superset in `scanA11y`, adding `<html lang>` and WCAG body-text contrast as advisory panel rows. Because `Warning` has no severity field, `check` fails on any a11y finding with no advisory tier and no opt-out.
- **Proposed better:** Make the diagnostic channel severity-aware: add a two-level `Severity { Error, Advisory }` to `Warning`, mark the a11y rules Advisory (matching the preview's own "never blocks" contract), and have `check` always report advisories but exit non-zero on them only under an explicit `--strict` (or `--a11y-strict`) opt-in, while true correctness errors (dangling xref, missing asset, unparseable YAML) always fail. Then close the preview-vs-gate coverage gap by adding the one high-value rule the gate can compute statically: a theme-token contrast check that resolves the default light and dark `--tali-*` foreground/background pairs from `render/theme.rs` and flags any pair below WCAG AA, with no browser and no kernel. Per-element inline-style contrast stays live-only, documented as the explicit boundary. Keep click-to-source and the corpus pin throughout.
- **Revised recommendation:** Split the entry and keep only the strong half. KEEP: add Severity { Error, Advisory } to Warning so a11y findings become distinguishable from correctness errors (a dangling xref renders wrong; an alt-less img renders fine but is less accessible) and can be selectively suppressed. That is the one genuinely load-bearing fix and it survives every invariant. RECONSIDER THE DEFAULT: the proposal reads the preview-vs-check split as a bug and downgrades check to advisory-by-default behind --strict. But the split is defensibly role-appropriate (advisory is right while drafting live; a pre-publish CI gate blocking is its job), and it clashes with the owner's clean-break strict-validator disposition (any unknown config key hard-fails). Sharper: keep a11y failing check by default, but use the new Severity to (a) label the findings ADVISORY in output so they read differently from a real error even while both fail, and (b) provide an explicit per-doc/CLI opt-out (a --no-a11y-gate escape hatch) rather than requiring --strict to turn enforcement ON. DROP OR DOWNSCOPE the static theme-token contrast rule: fold it into a unit test in theme.rs asserting the built-in light/dark/sepia pairs meet AA (a regression guard on author-owned constants that produces no user-facing, un-clickable diagnostic), and leave real contrast checking in the live preview where the browser computes it. That live-browser contrast check, run in the authoring loop, already IS Taliesin's genuine edge over Quarto per the steelman, so there is nothing to prove by half-reproducing it statically.
- **Tradeoffs:** Adding `Severity` touches every `Warning` construction site and the check/serve reporting paths: mechanical but wide. Defaulting a11y to advisory could clash with the author's strict-gate instinct (the clean-break config validator hard-fails on any unknown key), and some authors genuinely want a11y as a hard CI wall, which is why this is an explicit `--strict` opt-in rather than a silent downgrade. The theme-token contrast rule covers only Taliesin-owned theme pairs, not arbitrary inline `style="color:..."` (still live-only), and risks false positives on intentionally low-contrast decorative text, so it needs its own scope limit or escape hatch. More surface area to keep the corpus pin honest. (skeptic-found downside: The static theme-token contrast rule is the weak third of the proposal and has three problems the drafter missed. (1) Wrong source of truth and no user-owned source line: the tokens are not in render/theme.rs as the proposal states, they live in bundled assets/css/base.css and dark.css. A below-AA built-in pair is Taliesin's CSS, not the author's .tmd, so a located finding would have nowhere in the user's editable source to click to, and the fix is an edit to bundled CSS the user cannot make. (2) It re-checks the already-safe case and skips the risky one: base.css already hand-audits these pairs in comments (accent 3.20:1/2.41:1 -> accent-fill; muted darkened from 4.44:1 to 5.38:1 to pass AA), so a static pass over built-in tokens finds them all passing and adds value only as a rare-regression guard on a handful of author-controlled constants. The real contrast risk (custom theme: my.css, inline style="color:...") is explicitly left live-only, so the rule covers the safe case and skips the actionable one. (3) It needs a hand-curated list of which fg/bg pairs actually co-occur (fg-on-bg, muted-on-bg, link-on-bg, on-accent-on-accent-fill) or a naive cross-product produces meaningless pairs; that curated registry is ongoing maintenance duplicating what the live browser measures for free.)
- **Invariant check:** HTML-only: operates purely on the emitted HTML block model and static theme tokens, no new output format. Single read-only surface: findings navigate via click-to-source (file+line) and never write; the fixes (`alt=""`, `aria-label`, a theme edit) are source edits the author makes in the editor, not preview gestures. Keep-Markdown: no syntax change; rules read existing rendered HTML and standard attributes, and `![]()` already auto-emits `alt`. Click-to-source: every located finding stays on the shared `Warning` channel with file+line and remains the only bridge back to source. Block-level incremental: `scanA11y` already re-runs per op over the mounted DOM, static rules key off `block.html` + sourcepos, and `Severity` is just a field, so the data-block-id/data-sourcepos invariants are untouched. Warm server: the rules are kernel-free and theme-token contrast is a pure token computation with no browser and no per-edit startup cost. Corpus-plus-roadmap: already pinned by `corpus/diagnostics/a11y.qmd`; the severity and contrast extensions ship pinned by extending that doc plus its `check`-path tests. (possible violation flagged: No hard invariant is broken, but the static theme-token contrast rule strains click-to-source: a below-AA built-in pair lives in bundled base.css/dark.css, which is not the author's editable source, so the located-diagnostic channel would have no user-owned file+line to navigate to. A located warning that cannot point into the author's .tmd is off-contract for that channel (the fix is an edit to Taliesin's own CSS, not the source). The severity-field and warn-vs-fail parts violate nothing (HTML-only, read-only surface, Markdown syntax, block model, warm server, corpus pin all intact).)
